keywords.indexterm: License serverLicensing events in XML format

body.p: The license server also reports the individual licensing events that it recorded, at: http://hostName:port/oXygenLicenseServlet/license-events. An event says which user was granted, rejected, released, or timed out a license, when, and from which computer.

Use this report to find out who was denied a license and how often, for example to tell whether a single user retried many times or several different users were affected. The XML report only reports the total number of rejected requests, as a single counter.
body.note: This report is protected in the same way as the other license server management pages. You must use a user configured with the admin role, or with the manager role if you configured one.

section.title: Query Parameters

table.title: Parameters of the Licensing Events Report

row.entry: The type of the events to report: rejected, granted, released, timeout, or all.
Only the events that were recorded at this moment or later.
Only the events that were recorded before this moment.
Only the events that follow the event with this identifier. Use it to read the next page of a report that was truncated. It cannot be combined with groupBy.
Set it to user to report one row per user instead of one row per event.
The maximum number of rows to report. It must be at least 1, and larger values than 10000 are reduced to 10000.

section.p: The since and until parameters accept either a number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch (1755162723000) or a date in the ISO-8601 format (2026-08-14T09:12:03Z).

section.title: The Reported Events
section.p: For example, if the current moment is 14 August 2026, 09:00 UTC, then the users that were denied a license in the last day are reported by /license-events?since=2026-08-13T09:00:00Z:<licenseEvents type="rejected" returned="2" hasMore="true" oldest="2026-02-11T08:00:01Z" nextAfter="10230"> <event id="10229" time="2026-08-14T09:12:03Z" type="rejected" user="jdoe" hostname="jdoe-mbp" ip="10.1.2.3" mac="00:11:22:33:44:55" sessionId="node01ab7x9k2m" usedLicenses="50"/> <event id="10230" time="2026-08-14T09:12:04Z" type="rejected" user="asmith" hostname="asmith-pc" ip="10.1.2.9" mac="00:11:22:33:44:66" sessionId="node01qq2z8p4d" usedLicenses="50"/> </licenseEvents>

The licenseEvents element reports what was queried:
returned - The number of reported rows.
hasMore - Whether more events match the query than were reported. When the events are grouped by user, it reports whether more users were left out.
nextAfter - The value to pass as the after parameter to read the next page. It is missing when no event was reported.
oldest - The moment of the oldest event of this type that the license server still has. It is missing when it has none. It lets you tell an interval in which nothing happened from an interval that is older than the recorded history.

Each event element reports the identifier and the moment of the event, its type, the user name, the host name, the IP address, and the MAC address of the computer where Oxygen runs, the identifier of the session, and the number of licenses that were in use when the event was recorded. The attributes whose value the license server does not know are missing, rather than empty. For example, the events that were recorded by a license server older than version 29 have no sessionId.

The user attribute is the only one that is always present. When the client did not name the user that it requested a license for, the event is reported for the user (unknown-name), and the events of all such clients are counted together. For the events that were recorded by a license server older than version 29, it is the word user followed by the internal identifier of the user, as the name itself was not recorded at that time.
section.note: The events are never merged, and each of them has an identifier larger than the identifier of the events before it. To follow the events from a monitoring script, store the nextAfter value of a report and pass it as the after parameter of the next request. This way, each event is reported to you exactly once.

section.title: Events Grouped by User
section.p: The groupBy=user parameter counts the events of each user instead of reporting them one by one, the users with the most events first:<licenseEvents type="rejected" groupBy="user" returned="2" hasMore="false" oldest="2026-02-11T08:00:01Z"> <group user="jdoe" count="37"/> <group user="asmith" count="4"/> </licenseEvents>

In the example above, a single user accounts for 37 of the 41 denials, so the license server was most likely short of licenses for one person who retried, rather than for the whole team. The type, since, and until parameters select the events before they are counted, and limit caps the number of reported users.

ul.li: The events are reported only after a license key is activated on the license server, and only the events of the currently activated kind of license key are reported.
All the recorded events are removed when the kind of the activated license key changes.

On a license server that uses a named-user license key, the events of a user are also removed together with the user itself, that is when the Oxygen application reports that it did not use the license that it was granted, or when the user is no longer allowed to request a license. A floating license server never removes them.
